## Definitions

- [statement] Fee-free status is a per-market setting that Lighter has changed before. All RWA perp markets traded with 0 fees across every fee and staking tier in March 2026, and in April 2026 RWA market fees turned back on, applied based on tier. In April 2026 Lighter added is_taker_fee_enabled and is_maker_fee_enabled fields to the orderBookDetails endpoint so clients can verify markets where fees are disabled, and said only $LIT had maker fees set to zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-18) — https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/104 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/121, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/122
- [statement] A Lighter API key is a keypair separate from the Ethereum key. Each key is bound to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and has its own nonce stream. Usable key indexes are 4 to 254. Indexes 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's apps (on Robinhood Chain, 157 is also reserved), and 255 is only for querying all keys. Registering a key uses ChangePubKey, which always needs an L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/wasm-signer.md
- [statement] Variational's documented public API is a market-statistics REST endpoint (GET /metadata/v2/stats, 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP). An unofficial, reverse-engineered TypeScript client on GitHub says Variational publishes no trading API and no API keys, and warns its API can change without notice. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/technical-documentation/api · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/Magicianhax/variational-trading-api/blob/main/README.md

- [statement] An API key is a hot wallet. On 16 November 2026 one wallet withdrew about 10.39 million USDC from Lighter's contract (Bitquery on-chain trace); Lighter said a leaked API key for one trader's account caused it and that its protocol and smart contracts were unaffected. Lighter's postmortem said a trader's custom signing software reused nonces so the key could be computed from public signatures, and the attacker moved the victim's funds into a public pool and redeemed them. Lighter's Security Council returned about $5 million, withdrawals were later restored, wallet signature requirements were added for public-pool transfers, and IP allowlists and configurable API key permissions are planned. A Lighter API key can trade, cancel, modify, change leverage, manage sub-accounts and withdraw to its own L1 address. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-18) — https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://www.blockhead.co/2026/11/18/api-keys-are-the-new-hot-wallet-lighter-luxor-and-signalplus-show-how-credentials-beat-contracts/, https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/lighter-says-withdrawals-resume-after-api-key-theft, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md

## Structure and components

- [statement] Across MEXC, Phemex and BingX, zero-fee futures headlines come with API carve-outs. MEXC's Jun 1, 2026 notice sets an API schedule of 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker, and says API trading is subject to a separate fee structure that takes precedence over promotional offers such as 0-fee events. The Phemex carnival terms exclude API trading, and BingX's TradFi promotion excludes API trading. - [statement] MEXC's API futures fee notices say API trades follow a separate fee structure that takes precedence over web and app rates and over promotional offers such as 0-fee events and MX discounts. MEXC's own example: BTCUSDT futures cost maker 0% and taker 0.01% on the web or app, but trades executed via API are charged the API rate. - [statement] Gate's USDT-M TradFi Perpetuals have a dedicated fee structure effective September 1, 2026. VIP 0 pays 0.0200% maker and 0.0500% taker, and the maker fee is 0.0000% only at VIP 14, VIP 15 and VIP 16, with taker 0.0180%, 0.0150% and 0.0120%. Market-maker tiers pay 0.000% (MM 0) and -0.003%, -0.004% and -0.005% (MM 1 to MM 3). Gate's USDT-M Perpetual Futures Taker Program commences on September 1, 2026, with discounts of 9%, 16% and 20% for monthly taker volume shares of 0.02% ≤ X < 0.2%, 0.2% ≤ X < 1% and X ≥ 1%; participants contact their Account Manager to register. Gate's fee page says users whose API trading volume accounts for at least 60%, or who have reached VIP tier 15 or 16, will be automatically upgraded to advanced institutional users. It then raised the API schedule twice: to 0.04% maker and 0.06% taker effective May 1, 2026, at 08:00 (UTC) (notice listed Apr 30, 2026), and to 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker effective Jun 1, 2026, at 08:00 (UTC) (notice listed May 28, 2026). - [statement] RPI orders must be Post-Only, are guaranteed by the matching engine to match only Retail Taker orders, have the lowest execution priority at their price level, rest until cancelled, and are placed via the New Order endpoint with `instruction="RPI"`. The UI book can appear crossed because of RPI orders, while the API orderbook never contains them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles
- [statement] Order signing is computationally expensive. Paradex's best-practices page quotes 0.4ms (C++) and 0.2ms (Rust) average signing latency and advises pre-signing static order components, using the optional `market` parameter on cancel-by-client-id, and using the `bbo.{market_symbol}` WebSocket channel for price-only strategies. The Python SDK paradex-py supports L1 + L2 authentication. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/api/general-information/api-best-practices · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-py
- [statement] Hyperliquid ALO write priority (official docs): ALO orders are processed FIFO as transactions, with similar end-to-end latency as cancels, and all cancels are prioritized before all immediately executable orders. An optional ALO priority fee is charged from undelegated staking balance as a fraction of resting notional and is deducted at placement regardless of whether the order fills; on the timescale of 400ms it sorts only the tail of the queue at each level, made up of orders placed within the past 400ms. IOC priority has an effect of approximately 45 ms reduction in end-to-end latency per 1 bp of priority fee, linear from 0-8bps. A taker-signal strategy converted to ALO is handled in the cancel-speed lane, but paying for queue position costs money even when the order never fills (inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/priority-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide, https://multicoin.capital/2026/02/17/adverse-selection-rules-everything-around-me/
- [statement] Hyperliquid documents queue priority for ALO orders. On the timescale of 400ms, the tail of the queue at each level, made up of orders placed within the past 400ms, is sorted by priority rate. The rate is charged from undelegated staking balance as a fraction of resting notional in the case of ALO, and the fees are deducted at time of placing the order regardless of whether the order fills. ALO orders are processed FIFO as transactions with similar end-to-end latency as cancels. A third-party guide dates the ALO priority fee to July 2026; the official page read here carries no date for it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/priority-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide

Galaxy Research notes that US traders will get a separate, permissioned venue with its own clearing, and that the liquidity will not be shared with the existing HIP-3 markets, meaning the US venue will start from zero. - [statement] In a November 2026 announcement Lighter said new per-IP WebSocket limits take effect on Lighter Core after the scheduled downtime on Sunday, November 22. Standard / public, Plus and base Premium get 50 connections, 1,000 subscriptions, 200 unique accounts and 200 client messages per 60 seconds. Premium 1 and above get 255 connections, 5,000 subscriptions, 5,000 unique accounts and 1,000 client messages per 60 seconds; Builder gets 255, 10,000, 10,000 and 10,000. Only connections authenticated with the Authorization handshake header receive tier limits, while Plus and base Premium retain Standard limits even when authenticated. The rate-limits docs page still listed the older limits of 255 connections and 5000 subscriptions per IP. - [statement] On the morning of November 16 (UTC) an attacker recovered API private keys from public signatures because the affected accounts used unsafe signing code other than the official Lighter SDKs that reused signing nonces, then moved funds through a public pool: create a public pool from the affected account, mint pool shares in a separate attacker-controlled account, transfer the affected account's funds into the pool (increasing NAV without minting pool shares), redeem the shares and withdraw. Lighter says its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. Bitquery traced one withdrawal of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC to a single wallet that swapped it to ETH in four minutes and sent 1,920 ETH through twelve new wallets to Hyperliquid, where each one bought XMR1. (high confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/GoPlusSecurity/status/2122520900046319815, https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack, https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/11/16/lighter-suspends-all-withdrawals-after-usd10-4-million-crypto-exploit, https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/
- [statement] lighter-go v1.0.13 retracts v1.0.1 because GenerateAPIKey with a non-empty seed produced weak, predictable API keys, and tells users to upgrade and rotate any API key generated with a seed. The same release bumps golang.org/x/crypto for a critical vulnerability and requires Go 1.26. - [statement] Third-party connectors have had real-money defects on Lighter. The issue notes that trade-history polling queries the market-wide /api/v1/recentTrades endpoint, whose sample BTC-USDC response covered only ~9.5 seconds of market trades, so it can miss the account's fills; whether that happened for these two orders was not established. Bubblemaps says the attacker deposited $20k into Lighter and withdrew $10.39M about 36 minutes later. (high confidence) — https://x.com/bubblemaps/status/2122298877566931424 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack
- [statement] An API response with code 200 means the transaction was accepted, not executed. When the outcome is unknown (timeout, dropped connection, no WebSocket confirmation), do not re-sign blindly. Check the transaction status by hash or the account_tx channel, and compare nextNonce with the nonce used. Re-signing with a new nonce while the original may still execute can place the order twice. Reusing the same clientOrderIndex rejects a duplicate only while the first order is still open. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Lighter's troubleshooting page maps symptoms to causes. invalid nonce (21104): two processes use one API key concurrently, or an earlier transaction failed in the sequencer without consuming its nonce; batch nonces must be consecutive (21105). invalid PublicKey, please run changePubKey (21108): the key is not registered at that index, or another app replaced it at the same index. Signature rejected: the chainId must be 304 for mainnet and 300 for testnet. HTTP 429 or 405: rate limited, so back off, authenticate requests, reduce polling (use WebSocket) or change tier. account not found (21100) after a deposit: deposits take a few minutes to credit (CCTP: ~15–20 min). WebSocket disconnects come from no frame within 2 minutes, too many subscriptions, reading too slowly, or a server deployment. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can buy volume quota with USDC on Lighter mainnet through POST /api/v1/buyVolumeQuota at 0.0005 USDC per quota (1,000,000 quota = 500 USDC). A single request can buy at most 15,000,000 quota, and the balance after the purchase must not exceed 30,000,000; trading alone refills the balance only up to 15,000,000. The payment is an L2Transfer that you sign and pass as tx_info. lighter-python users should use client.sign_transfer() to obtain the signed tx_info and not client.transfer(), because it submits the transfer through sendTx, moving the payment asset without purchasing quota. The endpoint is not available on testnet. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/account/accountlimits.md

- [statement] Aster's recommended V3 futures API signs requests with an EIP-712 signature made with an API wallet ('signer'); the nonce uses microsecond precision and is valid only within a window of 60 seconds before and after server time, and each agent address maintains only the most recent 100 nonces. An optional nonceWindow (valid range 1 – 60000 milliseconds) causes a request the sequencer has not processed by nonce + nonceWindow to be rejected, returning code -4227. New V1 API key creation is no longer supported from March 25, 2026, but existing API keys continue to work. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation, https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs
- [statement] BULK's trading API uses Ed25519 signatures for state-mutating operations (official bulk-keychain library for Node, browser, Python and Rust). Public mainnet limits per client IP are 5 requests/second sustained with a 150-request burst for API requests and 5 actions/second with a 64-action burst for order actions through /api/v1/order; WebSocket allows 32 actions/second per connection (96-action burst) and 15 concurrent connections per client IP. BULK applies a 25 millisecond speed bump to transactions that may take liquidity, while transactions containing only provably maker-only orders proceed immediately; the docs call the speed bump a temporary launch mechanism limited to the first 90–120 days. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.bulk.trade/api-reference/introduction · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.bulk.trade/api-reference/rate-limits, https://docs.bulk.trade/architecture/taker-speed-bump

- [statement] Incident (official account): on Jan 19 a planned 30-minute database upgrade hit a race condition during a service restart, a corrupted state was persisted and published to Paradex Chain, and some markets reset the funding index to 0, creating abnormal funding PnL that triggered liquidations. Paradex rolled the chain back to block 1604710 (04:27:54 UTC), cancelled all open orders except TP/SL orders, and saw additional liquidations primarily on PAXG when aggressive orders skewed the mark price during the post-only period. Within 24 hours it refunded $650,000 across 200 accounts from the Liquidator Vault, called this Paradex Chain's first rollback, and added restart-procedure, data-validation, scale-up-process and post-only price-band safeguards. - [statement] Albers et al. conclude it is challenging to overcome the taker fee with taker strategies even when the signal has a robust pre-fee edge, and that maker strategies, despite not paying taker fees, do not offer an easy way around that because of queue position, fill probability and price drift. Their abstract says viable maker strategies often need to be contrarian to the prevailing order-book imbalance. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1
- [statement] A Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 1, 2026 shows a Hyperliquid close order submitted as a BUY LIMIT_MAKER on HYPE-USD rejected with 'Reduce only order would increase position'; this is a reduce-only reject, not a post-only cross reject, and the root cause was not established in the thread. (low confidence) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8269 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
- [statement] Albers et al. build a reversal model that predicts when the imbalance falsely signals the next move. Balanced-inventory maker trading gated by the logistic model at threshold 0.24 had 327 round trips per day and an average return of 0.71 bp per round trip, against an average loss of 0.44 bp (net of rebates) for the naive strategy; the Sharpe ratio improves from -109 to 11.97. The returns include a maker rebate on each leg of the roundtrip. The authors say the strategy is slightly profitable with min-sized orders and assuming low fees, albeit those profits are likely not scalable, and that it demonstrates a proof-of-concept. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
- [statement] Hyperliquid ALO rejections are routine in live bots. A Hyperliquid TWAP bot's mainnet logs for 2026-08-20..23 show 531 ALO rejections, all 'Post only order would have immediately matched', next to 2,305 resting ALOs. In another bot, when both ALO attempts are rejected the function returns before registering the IOC for the remainder, so the entry is abandoned silently, with no IOC and no fill line. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/howlrs/hype-trigger-twap/pull/53 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/rcerucci/hl-jev/issues/42, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/error-responses
- [statement] Bitnomial provides two methods for connecting and trading on the Exchange: Direct and Indirect. Direct Market Access (DMA) provides low-latency connectivity through private network connections, with AWS PrivateLink as the primary option. Its Binary (BTP) API is a low latency binary protocol for order entry and price feeds. The REST API is rate-limited to 200 requests per 5 minutes, and exceeding this rate results in HTTP 403 responses. - [statement] Hyperliquid enforces its US restriction at the front end, not the chain. As of November 2, 2026 the frontend at app.hyperliquid.xyz still showed its restricted-jurisdiction banner to a US connection, and the Terms of Service still restricted use by US persons. The L1 protocol underneath does not perform this check; it processes signed transactions from any wallet. Per the guide, Hyperliquid's own Terms of Service are the actual restriction, and the frontend IP check is one mechanism for enforcing them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://hyperliquidguide.com/privacy/hyperliquid-us-availability · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/terms
- [statement] A taker-side delay is a transfer, not a free lunch, and who ends up paying depends on maker competition. Multicoin: delay-based methods do not eliminate toxic order flow but determine where it appears and who pays, and toxic flow raises spreads for everyone. Baldauf and Mollner (CEPR VoxEU): delaying non-cancellation orders improves conditions for liquidity providers, and competition among them will likely pass some or all of the gain to other traders as tighter, deeper quotes. This is a model prediction, not a measured result for Lighter. (medium confidence) — https://multicoin.capital/2026/02/17/adverse-selection-rules-everything-around-me/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/asymmetric-speed-bumps-market-design-response-high-frequency-trading
- [statement] Moving money is not free even when trading is. Variational charges a flat $0.1 per deposit or withdrawal. On Lighter, account-to-account transfers and fast withdrawals use the transferFeeInfo endpoint, and the fee is charged on top of the amount. A fast withdrawal is USDC-only with a 4 USDC minimum, while a secure withdrawal goes only to the owner's own L1 address and settles via Ethereum. DefiLlama lists transfer and withdrawal fees among Lighter's protocol revenue. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/omni/trading/fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/deposits-transfers-and-withdrawals, https://api.llama.fi/summary/fees/lighter

## How-to and procedures

The discounted fee amount is in the fill's `fee` field. - [statement] KCEX's blog gives a cost example for a strategy trading $10 million in monthly futures notional through an API, with 60% maker and 40% taker executions. At 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker it computes $6 million × 0.0006 = $3,600 plus $4 million × 0.0008 = $3,200, totaling $6,800. If a trader mistakenly modeled both sides at 0.01%, expected commission would be only $1,000, understating cost by $5,800. - [statement] Standard accounts have 300ms taker latency, 300ms cancel latency and 0ms post-only latency. Premium removes the delay on cancels and post-only placement and sets the taker delay at 140ms. A batch waits for the longest speed bump of any transaction in it, so mixing a taker order into a batch of post-only orders delays all of them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees
- [statement] API trading uses transactions signed with SignerClient and sent with the sendTx or sendTxBatch REST endpoints, or the jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch WebSocket types. A batch holds up to 50 transactions from the same account and API key with consecutive nonces. REST batches of up to ~15 orders are safe because request-body size limits at the CDN edge can reject a large REST batch; WebSocket messages are limited to 64 KB. A response of code: 200 only means the transaction was accepted, so subscribe to account_orders/{market}/{account} or account_tx/{account} to see fills and rejections. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting, https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/blob/main/lighter/signer_client.py, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md

- [statement] Common Lighter API errors and fixes: invalid nonce (21104) means two processes use one API key concurrently or an earlier transaction failed in the sequencer without consuming its nonce, so refetch nextNonce and re-sign; batch nonces must be consecutive (21105); invalid PublicKey, please run changePubKey (21108) means the key is not registered or was replaced by another app using the same index; the chainId must be 304 for mainnet and 300 for testnet; HTTP 429 or 405 means rate limited; WebSocket drops come from no frame within 2 minutes (send pings every ~60 s and reconnect automatically); account not found (21100) after a deposit usually means deposits take a few minutes to credit (CCTP: ~15–20 min). - [statement] Delta Tech Systems' latency study (published 20 April 2026) sampled eleven venues, with each region run for five minutes. It found Extended had a p50 of 50–130 ms but a bimodal tail with p95 of 13–40 seconds and a max of 38–59 seconds, a pattern that looks like periodic server-side buffering and burst delivery, and called it unusable as a real-time reference until fixed upstream. Five minutes is short for tail statistics, so retest before relying on or dismissing Extended's stream. - [statement] Pacifica's API uses credit quotas over 60s: an unidentified IP gets 100 credits and a valid API config key 300, and quotas rise with fee tier (tier 1 300, tier 2 600, tier 3 1200, tier 4 2400, tier 5 6000, VIP1 12000, VIP2 24000, VIP3 30000); the credit is shared across a main account and all its subaccounts. A standard action costs 1 credit, a cancel 0.5, and heavy GET requests 3-12 (1-4 with a config key); exhausted credits return HTTP 429 and the ratelimit and ratelimit-policy response headers show the balance. WebSocket limits include 255 concurrent connections per IP and 500 subscriptions per connection. Each account can hold 300 open orders per market at fee tier 1 and 1,000 at fee tier 2 and above and for market makers. Requests are signed by API Agent Keys (Agent Wallets) with agent_wallet added to the request header, and a Python SDK example for agent keys exists. - [statement] Veranta's docs describe two official SDKs (Python `veranta-sdk` and TypeScript). The recommended API key is a delegate key, a separate key registered to the wallet that can trade but can never withdraw funds, approve USDC or add other delegates, registered with one wallet signature via the Veranta API Key Generator. The Veranta relayer puts the order on-chain and pays the gas, so no ETH, no node and no contract ABIs are needed. Nonces are an unordered bitmap and any unused 256-bit value works; clients should call GET /v2/meta at startup. The SDK repo's latest commit message mentions 200 ms receipt polling. - [statement] Polymarket Perps shows near-zero fees drifting upward. - [statement] On a Lighter Standard account regular perpetual orders pay 0 maker and 0 taker fee, so converting a taker entry to post-only saves no fee; the only gain is the spread not crossed (plus slippage on size). - [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills: between deciding to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine the order can still get filled, and those fills are the worst because the market is about to run through the quote. - [statement] Official fee schedules: Paradex Retail pays 0% maker and taker; Paradex Pro pays a flat 0.005% (0.5 bps) maker against a taker fee of 0.045% at the base tier, floored at 1.75 bps after discounts; Hyperliquid tier 0 pays 0.015% maker against 0.045% taker. - [statement] Paradex keeps two books. The UI and interactive-token (Retail) orders see RPI liquidity, which only Retail takers can match, which must be post-only and which has the lowest priority at its price. The API book excludes RPI, so a Pro (default API) post-only order rests in a book without RPI quotes. OpenChainBench reports that the two books can diverge on thin pairs (SOL on 2026-09-22: 0.03 % spread on the interactive book against 1.4 % on the API book; a single-day vendor figure). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://openchainbench.com/benchmarks/perp-fees
- [statement] Latency must be in the simulator. Albers et al. say their imbalance-strategy comparison ignores latency, 'potentially leading to an overstatement of results'. a vendor article says simulators that seed queue position at decision time overestimate queue priority by the volume that arrives during the latency window. For these venues the inputs follow the docs (inference): Lighter Standard 0 ms maker latency and 300 ms cancel/modify and taker latency; Paradex Retail 300ms for submission and cancellation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/, https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/Market%20Making%20with%20Alpha%20-%20Order%20Book%20Imbalance.html, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Published maker-with-signal results are rebate-dependent. The hftbacktest tutorial's order-book-imbalance market maker (Binance BTCUSDT) bases its backtests on a 0.005% rebate; its return per trade drops from 0.0139% to 0.0086% including the 0.005% rebates in February 2025 after the power_prob_queue_model parameter was changed from 2 to 3 to reflect a more challenging fill in the queue. The author says this highlights the importance of rebates. Albers et al.'s gated rows also include a maker rebate on each leg of the roundtrip. (medium confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/Market%20Making%20with%20Alpha%20-%20Order%20Book%20Imbalance.html · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Re-pegging by amend resets queue priority. A vendor article states that on virtually every crypto venue an amend is a cancel/replace that returns a new order ID at the back of the queue, so a quoting engine that re-pegs every 500ms is perpetually re-entering at the back. NautilusTrader's docs say Hyperliquid modifies orders by cancel-replace: the modify action cancels the original order (old oid) and opens a replacement with a new oid. Moallemi and Yuan find that adverse selection costs increase with queue position. A chase-style conversion loop therefore trades fill rate against priority. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/integrations/hyperliquid/, https://moallemi.com/ciamac/papers/queue-value-2016.pdf
- [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills. A vendor article says fills that arrive between the decision to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine are the worst fills, because the market was about to run through the quote, and a simulator without cancel latency deletes exactly those fills. Lighter Standard (300 ms cancel/modify) and Paradex Retail (300ms cancellation speed bump) both impose that window by design; Lighter Premium/Advanced and Paradex Pro do not. Inference: the effect applies on these venues but has not been measured on them. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Conversion pays only if the fee gap plus the spread saved beats adverse drift and missed trades, so the fee tier decides. Lighter Standard accounts pay 0 maker and 0 taker on regular perpetual orders. Lighter Premium/Advanced at zero staked LIT pays 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker. Hyperliquid's base perpetual tier pays 0.015% maker and 0.045% taker. Against that, Daru measured negative 10-second pre-fee entry markouts for a touch quoter (-0.39 to -0.84 bp across Bybit, Binance USD-M and Hyperliquid), and its Bybit depth panel finds no level profitable per quoting opportunity below a 0.328 bp rebate. This is an inference from fee tables and third-party markouts, not a measurement on these venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees, https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] In the hl-jev bot the ALO rests and an IOC after 8 s takes the remainder. Its first logged entry fill (buy 0.11 @ 121.73) had fill_role: taker, so the IOC fallback, not the resting ALO, supplied that fill. In practice a converted strategy becomes a maker-first, taker-fallback hybrid, and its realised fee and slippage mix depends on the timeout. (low confidence) — https://github.com/rcerucci/hl-jev/issues/42 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
- [statement] Re-pegging a post-only order is a cost lever, not free maintenance. A vendor article says a price amend is a cancel/replace on virtually every crypto venue that returns a new order ID at the back of the queue, so a quoter that re-pegs every 500ms is perpetually re-entering at the back. In Daru's simulation, loosening the re-quote condition removes at least 28.5% of the measured adverse selection on Bybit and 32.7% on Hyperliquid (a floor, not a point estimate), so frequent re-posting adds adverse selection. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/DaruFinance/crypto-adverse-selection, https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] Cancel latency makes the worst fills. Between the decision to pull a quote and the cancel reaching the matching engine the order can still get filled, and the vendor article says those fills are the worst because the market was about to run through the quote. Albers et al. state that ignoring latency can overstate their strategy results. Applied to Lighter Standard's 300ms cancel latency or Paradex Retail's 300ms cancellation speed bump, this is an inference, not a measurement on those venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles

- [statement] Paradex says it earns from RPI maker flow, not from retail takers. Professional makers post RPI orders that are visible in the UI and hidden from the API. These match only against Retail takers, and the makers pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills; the Pro maker fee in the current docs is a flat 0.005%. Paradex calls the model analogous to TradFi payment for order flow (PFOF). An SEC DERA staff working paper (January 2025) measured PFOF rates of about 35 bps in crypto markets, against 8 bps for options and 0.8 bps for equities in prior work, and attributes the premium to crypto order flow being highly uninformed. Multicoin gives the same logic: makers lose to informed flow and earn the spread on uninformed flow. - [statement] TradFi evidence shows a zero commission can hide an execution-price cost that no fee page reveals. - [statement] Reported volume on points-driven zero-fee venues is a weak measure of real activity. Volume-to-open-interest turnover for Lighter was 8.03, against 1.57 for Hyperliquid, 5.4 for Aster and 2.7 for EdgeX (Stacy Muur). Castle Labs measured 2.87x a day for Lighter against 1.16x for Hyperliquid in its data for 17 August to 15 September 2026, and 7x to 9x for Jupiter Perps, Pacifica and GMTrade. Formo, using a DefiLlama snapshot of November 8, 2026, computed about 3.6x for Lighter, 2.6x for Variational and 1.1x for Hyperliquid and Aster. Formo says a high ratio is not proof of wash trading because venue design and fees differ. The open-source delta-farmer bot automates hedged volume creation for points programs on Lighter, Variational's Omni, Pacifica and other venues. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/32546519515305 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://castlelabs.io/research/reports/mapping-the-perpetual-trading-ecosystem, https://formo.so/blog/perp-dex-analytics-kpis, https://github.com/vladkens/delta-farmer
- [statement] Zero is measured against Hyperliquid's schedule. Hyperliquid's base perp rate is 0.045% taker and 0.015% maker. It falls with trailing volume to 0.024% taker and 0.000% maker above $7B. HYPE-staking tiers cut fees by up to 40% (above 500,000 HYPE staked), and maker rebates of -0.001% to -0.003% go to the largest maker-volume shares. TrueHold computes a $10,000 market-order round trip at $9 on Hyperliquid's base tier, $5.60 on Lighter Premium before discounts and $0 on Lighter Standard. Compare any zero-fee venue with the fee tier you would really hold, not the base rate. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees, https://openchainbench.com/benchmarks/perp-fees

- [statement] MEXC's official Futures API provides REST API and WebSocket streaming services. Order placement is POST /api/v1/private/order/create with the required permission Order Placing. Order type 2 is Post Only (maker only), alongside limit, IOC, FOK and market types, and stpMode sets the self-trade prevention mode. Accounts that have not completed KYC can still create an API key but may not be able to enable or use futures order placement–related permissions. API Keys that are not bound to IP addresses are valid for 90 days. Signing uses the HMAC-SHA256 algorithm with a Request-Time header, and a request is invalid if req_time is more than 10 seconds (default) behind or ahead of the server time. - [statement] On Lighter mainnet the Plus tier is the opt-in tier for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits. - [statement] REST limits depend on tier. Standard accounts get 60 requests per rolling minute, unweighted, with no separate sendTx bucket. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and read-only endpoints fall into a separate bucket from sendTx and sendTxBatch. Builder accounts, free of charge on application through Discord, get 240,000 weighted requests per rolling minute. Limits apply to both IP address and L1 address, and authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405, and a firewall block lasts 60 seconds. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/119, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/100
- [statement] On a Standard account every call competes for the same 60 requests per minute, including nonce and reconciliation reads, and weight-3,000 endpoints permit only eight calls/minute. Opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) also counts against the REST limit, and once it is exhausted new WebSocket connections receive HTTP 429. NautilusTrader suggests 15 transaction requests and 5 REST calls/minute for bounded Standard testing, and a Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 18, 2026 reports repeated 429 Too Many Requests errors on the Lighter perpetual private websocket connection and candle polling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8309
- [statement] API keys belong to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and each has its own key pair and nonce. Indexes 0–254 exist, 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's web/mobile apps, and 255 is a special index only for querying apikeys. Registering a key requires the L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). A key can trade, cancel, modify, change leverage and margin, create sub-accounts, make secure withdrawals (which can only go back to the L1 address that created the account) and make same-owner transfers. It cannot alone transfer to another L1 owner, fast-withdraw or approve an integrator with fees. Auth tokens last at most 8 hours, and Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md
- [statement] Premium/Advanced accounts can mark up to 251 API keys per account index as maker-only. These keys are restricted to 0ms speed bump transactions only (post-only (ALO) orders, modifies of ALO orders, cancel and cancel all) and get an optimized execution path with reduced scheduling latency. Order types with a speed bump sent via a maker-only key are rejected with error 62007, a 1-hour cooldown applies between api key type changes (error 62008), and Standard accounts are rejected (error 62009). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/114
- [statement] Each API key has its own transaction nonce, by default previous plus one, and the SkipNonce attribute allows jumps that stay below `2^47 - 1`. When a transaction fails without consuming its nonce, any transactions already sent on the same key with higher nonces fail too and must be re-signed starting from the current `nextNonce`. Failures while the sequencer applies the transaction (invalid size or price, duplicate `clientOrderIndex`, wrong reduce-only direction) do consume the nonce. An `invalid nonce` (21104) error can come from two processes using the same API key concurrently, so use one key per process, or serialize. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/112
- [statement] Order parameters: price is an integer scaled by 10^price_decimals and, for taker orders, is the worst acceptable price (the order is cancelled if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price); timeInForce is 0 Immediate-or-cancel, 1 Good-till-time or 2 Post-only; orderExpiry is a Unix ms timestamp between 5 minutes and 30 days ahead, with 0 for IOC orders; clientOrderIndex is a uint48 unique across all markets. The minimum order is the larger of min_base_amount and min_quote_amount. (medium confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting

- [statement] A leaked key that can trade can still lose money. - [statement] Lighter's first serious outage ran 4.5 hours, from 10:30PM EST on October 10, 2025 until 3AM EST on October 11, 2025, since mainnet private beta in January and public launch on October 1. - [statement] Lighter states that an API key can't withdraw funds to anyone else's wallet, because withdrawals only ever go to the account owner's own wallet. It also states that a key that can trade can still lose money for its owner if someone else holds it. Besides the pool route, Lighter names two risks. Someone holding the key could place orders from the account that trade against their own orders at bad prices, which works best in thinly traded markets. They could also open large or highly leveraged positions that expose the account to heavy losses or liquidation. - [statement] Lighter's docs list what an API key can do alone: trade, cancel, modify, leverage/margin, sub-accounts, secure withdrawals, same-owner transfers, and auth-gated REST and WebSocket reads. Secure withdrawals only need the API key because they can only go back to the L1 address that created the account. Alone it cannot make transfers to another L1 owner, fast withdrawals or approve an integrator with fees; a Transfer needs an L1 signature when sender and receiver have different owners, and ApproveIntegrator needs one when the integrator has a different owner and at least one max fee is > 0. Transfers between the same owner's accounts need no L1 signature. After the November 16 incident, Lighter also requires a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/wasm-signer.md, https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122394446343946717
- [statement] Premium/Advanced accounts can mark up to 251 API keys per account index as maker-only. These keys are restricted to 0ms speed bump transactions only (post-only (ALO) orders, modifies of ALO orders, cancel and cancel all) and have an optimized execution path that skips the speed-bump queue. Keys reserved by the front-end (0-3) cannot be set as maker-only, and a one-hour cooldown applies between changes. The setMakerOnlyApiKeys and getMakerOnlyApiKeys endpoints set and list maker-only keys. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/llms.txt
- [statement] Lighter queues transactions per API key, and each transaction waits for a speed bump before it executes (for example, on Standard, taker orders wait 300 ms and post-only orders 0 ms). A slow transaction delays everything sent after it on the same key: a post-only order sent right after a taker order on the same key waits for the taker order's 300 ms. A batch waits for the longest speed bump of any transaction in it, so mixing a taker order into a batch of post-only orders delays all of them. Lighter's guidance is a dedicated key per workload, for example one for quoting/cancelling, one for taking, one for transfers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] Each Lighter API key has its own transaction nonce, by default new_nonce = previous_nonce + 1. The SkipNonce attribute allows a jump if the new nonce exceeds the previous one; a skip-nonce jump must stay below 2^47 - 1 and the absolute nonce cap is 2^48 - 1. A rejection by the API server (bad signature, wrong nonce, rate limit, ExpiredAt less than ~5 s away, not enough margin for a resting order) does not consume the nonce, and neither does a sequencer rejection before the transaction is applied. Rejections while the sequencer applies the transaction (invalid size or price, duplicate clientOrderIndex, wrong reduce-only direction, cancelling or modifying an unknown order) do consume it. When a transaction fails without consuming its nonce, the higher-nonce transactions already sent on that key fail too, so re-sign from the current nextNonce. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/going-to-production/troubleshooting.md
- [statement] Order and batch field rules, from Lighter's signing guide: orderExpiry is a Unix ms timestamp between 5 minutes and 30 days ahead, and 0 for IOC orders. clientOrderIndex is a uint48 (at most 2^48−1) that is unique across all markets. For taker orders, price is the worst acceptable price: if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price, the order is cancelled. A batch holds up to 50 transactions from the same account and API key with consecutive nonces. REST batches of up to ~15 orders are safe because request-body size limits at the CDN edge can reject a large REST batch; WebSocket jsonapi/sendtxbatch accepts messages up to 64 KB, enough for 50 orders. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] WebSocket rules from Lighter's docs: clients must send at least one frame every 2 minutes (a WebSocket ping frame or any application-level message; {"type":"ping"} returns {"type":"pong"}). Writes to slow clients time out after 250 ms by default, so reconnect and resubscribe for fresh snapshots. Subscribe requests use slash-separated channel names while response channel values use colons. The order book channel sends new orders in batches every 50ms and a complete snapshot on subscription; a client can verify continuity by checking that begin_nonce on the current update matches the nonce of the previous update. Private channels take an auth token inside the subscribe message, while public-pool data does not require authentication. jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch send transactions over the websocket. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/websocket.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] On Standard accounts the limit of 60 requests per rolling minute is unweighted and covers transactions too: Standard accounts have no separate sendTx bucket and are still bound to the 60 requests per minute limit. The Transaction Type Limits table (default 40 requests per minute; L2Withdraw 2 per minute and 3 per 2 hours) applies to all account types. For Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts, each sendTx or sendTxBatch request costs 6 weight from a separate bucket, a batch counts as one request, and no IP limits are enforced, only L1 address limits. Builder accounts raise only the read-only limits; otherwise standard account limits apply. Opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) counts against the REST rate limit, and when that limit is exhausted new WebSocket connections receive HTTP 429. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/blob/3351adad0a09f6a57a202219d3e52fe794672421/hummingbot/connector/exchange/lighter/lighter_constants.py

- [statement] Paradex's best-practices page advises: sign orders natively (0.4ms C++, 0.2ms Rust average) and pre-sign static order components; use batch order endpoints (a single batch request = 1 rate limit unit regardless of 1-50 orders); pass the optional market parameter on cancel-by-client-id and cancel-all; avoid client IDs when possible; use the bbo.{market_symbol} WebSocket channel for price-only strategies; drain WebSocket messages quickly (the exchange disconnects if 2000+ messages accumulate); synchronize the clock using time.aws.com; and poll GET /v1/system/state, which returns ok, maintenance or cancel_only. - [statement] Maker fills coincide with adverse price moves. DeLise proves and measures a negative drift of a limit order fill (10 Year US Treasury Bond futures). Albers et al. document, in a live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual, a negative correlation between a maker order's fill probability and its subsequent return, because an order at the top of the queue fills with probability 1 when the next price move is against it. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2
- [statement] Lighter latency asymmetry: Standard accounts have taker latency 300ms, maker latency 0ms and cancel/modify latency 300ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have no added latency on cancels or Post Only placements and 140 ms taker latency. A maker-converted strategy on a Standard account can post instantly but cannot pull a stale quote for 300ms. - [statement] Backtests of a maker-converted strategy that assume a fill whenever price touches the limit overstate results. A worked example by a market-data vendor (plain symmetric maker, one month BTCUSDT perpetual) moves from +$9,600 under touch-fill to -$700 under a calibrated queue-depletion model, with a live shadow run at -$1,150; Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang found hypothetical first-passage executions are very poor proxies for actual limit-order executions. The vendor figures are a constructed illustration of a market maker, not a signal-taker conversion. - [statement] Touch-fill backtests overstate maker and maker-converted results. Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang find hypothetical limit-order executions built from first-passage times or transaction data are very poor proxies for actual limit-order executions. DeLise shows that backtest simulations using synthetic data and random-fill assumptions appear to be profitable but in reality fail to produce a profit. Freqtrade's backtester documents that all orders are filled at the requested price as long as the price is within the candle's high/low range. A vendor worked example on one BTCUSDT perpetual month moves from +$9,600 (touch on 1m bars) to -$700 (calibrated queue-depletion) against -$1,150 in a live shadow run. (high confidence) — https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1, https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/backtesting/, https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/
- [statement] Bar-based backtests cannot order events inside a bar. Claeys measured that 18.47% of 2,064,460 one-minute E-mini NASDAQ-100 bars (from 2020 through 2025) are ambiguous for a 10-point stop and 10-point target scalp, with a best-case to worst-case gap of 3,695 NQ points ($73,900) per 1,000 trades, and five platforms resolve the ambiguity differently. Freqtrade's docs say backtesting can never be perfect and 'will always be biased in one way or the other'. A converted entry whose limit, stop and target sit in one bar has the same ambiguity (futures evidence, not perps). (medium confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm?abstractid=6240638&mirid=1&type=2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/backtesting/
- [statement] Signal type decides whether post-only conversion can work. Albers et al. say viable maker strategies often require a contrarian approach, counter-trading the prevailing order book imbalance. Moallemi and Yuan find that adverse selection costs increase with queue position, and DeLise finds that limit order fills are caused by and coincide with adverse price movements. Inference: continuation or momentum entries convert poorly, fade or mean-reversion entries convert better. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://moallemi.com/ciamac/papers/queue-value-2016.pdf, https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1
- [statement] Fill probability falls steeply as the order moves away from the touch, while per-fill drift improves only modestly. Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang find execution times very sensitive to limit price. On a separate sample of 300 Bybit coin-days (buy side only), Daru's net per fill improves from -0.72 bp at the touch to -0.33 bp at the fifth level, but fills far less often, at 12% of the touch's rate. Inference: for a signal with a short half-life, a deeper post-only entry mostly turns into a missed trade. (medium confidence) — https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://daru.finance/research/crypto-adverse-selection
- [statement] Hyperliquid's Chase order is a Post Only (ALO) limit order that re-prices to track the best bid or ask. It rests one tick above the best bid (buys) or one tick below the best ask (sells), or at the best bid/ask when the spread is a single tick. It runs in the browser tab where it was created, up to 5 can be active, and it terminates on a rejection (for example below minimum notional or insufficient margin), when the limit order it placed is modified, when the tab is closed or refreshed, when the active address is switched, or when the same address is connected in another browser. The exchange endpoint documents limit orders (tif Alo, Ioc or Gtc) and trigger orders, so an API bot should expect to run its own cancel/replace loop (inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/order-types · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/support/faq/trade-outcome-looks-incorrect/why-was-my-chase-order-canceled, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint
- [statement] Hyperliquid rate limits for cancel/replace loops: the address-based limit allows 1 request per 1 USDC traded cumulatively since address inception, with an initial buffer of 10000 requests; when rate limited, an address is allowed one request every 10 seconds; cancels have cumulative limit min(limit + 100000, limit * 2); the default open order limit is 1000 plus one additional order for every 5M USDC of volume, capped at a total of 5000 open orders. A fresh account that re-pegs aggressively can burn its buffer quickly (inference) but keeps extra cancel headroom. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/rate-limits-and-user-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide
- [statement] Daru's makercex command-line tool (makercex measure --snapshots book.parquet --trades tape.parquet --horizon 10s) measures the entry markout of a passive quote against true-aggressor-signed tape, with cluster-robust intervals that abstain when the panel cannot support one. - [statement] Hyperliquid modify race: modifying a resting ALO order to a price that would cross cancels the original and then rejects the replacement as post-only, leaving no order. NautilusTrader's docs say an executable ALO or GTC replacement can cancel the original limit order before Hyperliquid rejects the replacement, and 'A modify rejection does not prove that the original order is still open.' A MetaMask issue reports a testnet run where a real ALO buy edited across the spread returned 'Error placing new order during modify: Post only order would have immediately matched, bbo was 2344.8@2345.2.' and orderStatus then reported the original order canceled. - [statement] Fills on a resting limit order are not a random sample of the market. DeLise proves a negative drift for limit-order fills and confirms it on 10 Year US Treasury Bond futures. In a one-week live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual (232,897 minimum-sized maker orders, of which 127,051 filled), Albers et al. find that fill probability and post-fill return are negatively correlated, with a negative expected return of approximately -0.8 bp (-0.3 bp net of rebate). In Lalor and Swishchuk's table for a basic posting strategy on four CME futures (single April 2024 days), for example ES had 767 adverse fills of 941. A post-only entry therefore tends to fill when the market is moving through it. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.16527v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2409.12721
- [statement] Post-only means cancel-on-cross, not re-price. Lighter automatically cancels a Post-Only order if crossing orders exist at placement. Paradex cancels a post-only order that would immediately match. Hyperliquid rejects a crossing ALO with error type BadAloPx, 'Post only order would have immediately matched, bbo was {bbo}'. A converted strategy therefore gets a cancel or a reject, not a fill, whenever its limit price is marketable on arrival, and it needs a defined next step for that case. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/order-types-and-matching · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/orders/order-instructions, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/error-responses, https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide
- [statement] The ability to pull a stale quote differs by venue and account type. Hyperliquid processes all cancels before all immediately executable orders, even orders with order priority. Lighter Standard accounts have 0ms maker latency but 300ms cancel/modify latency and 300ms taker latency; Lighter Premium/Advanced accounts have no additional latency on cancels or Post Only placements. Paradex Retail orders face a 300ms speed bump on submission and on cancellation; default API (Pro) orders have none. A converted strategy on Lighter Standard can post at once but cannot withdraw for 300ms. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/priority-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://multicoin.capital/2026/02/17/adverse-selection-rules-everything-around-me/, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] Lighter queues every transaction per API key behind a speed bump. On Standard, taker orders wait 300 ms and post-only orders 0 ms. A slow transaction delays everything sent after it on the same key: a post-only order sent right after a taker order on the same key waits for the taker order's 300 ms. A maker-first strategy with an IOC fallback should therefore use a dedicated key per workload, one for quoting/cancelling and one for taking. Premium/Advanced accounts can use maker-only API keys, which skip the speed-bump queue entirely. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Hyperliquid's Chase order is a Post Only (ALO) limit order that re-prices to track the best bid or ask. It rests one tick above the best bid (buys) or one tick below the best ask (sells), or at the best bid/ask when the spread is a single tick. It runs in the browser tab where it was created (up to 5 active) and ends on a rejection, on modification of the placed limit order, on tab close or refresh, on an address switch, or when the same address connects in another browser. The pages read here describe no API-level chase order, so an API bot builds its own re-pricing loop (inference). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/support/faq/trade-outcome-looks-incorrect/why-was-my-chase-order-canceled · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/order-types, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint
- [statement] A re-quoting loop spends Hyperliquid's address-based request budget: one request per 1 USDC traded cumulatively since address inception plus an initial buffer of 10000 requests, one request every 10 seconds once limited, and a cumulative limit for cancels of min(limit + 100000, limit * 2). During high congestion, addresses are limited to use their previous day maker share percentage of the block space. By inference, a strategy that traded only as a taker the day before has little block space in congestion. A third-party guide says 'twice' the previous day's maker share; the official page read here does not. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/rate-limits-and-user-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://hyperliquidguide.com/guides/trading/hyperliquid-market-making-guide
- [statement] Closing a position with a post-only order can fail for a reason other than crossing. Hyperliquid's documented ReduceOnly error is 'Reduce only order would increase position'. A Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 1, 2026 shows it returned for a BUY LIMIT_MAKER close order on HYPE-USD; the thread does not establish the cause. A maker-converted exit needs its own reject handling. (medium confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/error-responses · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8269
- [statement] Touch-fill assumptions overstate passive results. Lo, MacKinlay and Zhang find that hypothetical executions built from first-passage times or from transaction data are very poor proxies for actual limit-order executions: the mean lower-bound execution time understates the mean actual execution time and the upper-bound execution time overstates it. Lalor and Swishchuk say simulations that treat price and market-order arrivals as independent can largely inflate short-term strategy performance. A market-data vendor's worked example (one month of BTCUSDT perpetual, a constructed illustration) falls from +$9,600 under touch fills to -$700 under a calibrated queue-depletion model, against -$1,150 in a live shadow run; the quote fill rate falls from 89% to 37% (live 35%). (high confidence) — https://rodneywhitecenter.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/9912-.pdf · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.12721, https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/
- [statement] Crypto.com's US perps trade on a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse that does business in the Crypto.com App under the brand Crypto.com | Derivatives North America (CDNA) and in a separate trader-focused App, with leverage up to 5x, and the final funding rate cannot be higher than +2% or lower than −2% for an eight-hour interval. Foris DAX Inc is the entity registered with NFA as an introducing broker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://robinhood.com/newsroom/robinhood-cryptocom/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees · also: https://crypto.com/en/product-news/crypto-perpetuals-launch, https://help.crypto.com/en/articles/17741688-perpetual-trading-in-the-us, https://crypto.com/en/company-news/ogcom-and-cryptocom-expand-derivatives-offering-with-launch-of-regulated-crypto-perpetuals-for-the-us-market
- [statement] Kalshi's Perps API mirrors its event-contract API under a `/margin` namespace, with endpoints for account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, subaccounts, and transfers between event-contract and margin balances. Production endpoints are 'rolling out member by member', with REST on the `external-api` hosts and WebSocket and FIX on separate perps hosts. The event-contract to margin transfer is not yet available (enabled with the production rollout), and `/margin/enabled` shows whether margin is on for an account. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.kalshi.com/margin · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, US-person access to perpetuals and US-regulated perp fees
- [statement] Gibson Dunn says the risk controls it describes are principally associated with offshore and onchain trading venues, which generally are not available to US persons. CoinGape says Binance Futures, Bybit, Deribit, and OKX's international derivatives platform restrict US residents from using their international futures services. - [statement] US-based Kalshi users who have completed KYC verification are eligible to apply for perps access, and international availability may expand in the future. Applying involves a margin account application with a short questionnaire about trading experience and risk tolerance. Most retail users trade perpetuals currently through Kalshi Prime, a registered Futures Commission Merchant (FCM), while institutional participants may become Self-Clearing Members and clear directly with Kalshi Klear. - [statement] Kalshi documents a Perps API under a `/margin` namespace that mirrors its event-contract API. The production REST base URL is `https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/margin/` (rolling out member by member); WebSocket and FIX use separate perps hosts, and a lower-latency host serves fill and user_orders updates. Margin endpoints cover account balance and risk, funding (estimated and historical rates, plus payment history), fee tiers, and subaccounts. - [statement] Variational's economics are reported (BlockBeats) as a 4-6 bp spread charged to users against 0-2 bp hedging cost, with OLP annualised returns above 300% in Apr-Jul 2025. The article says hedging cost could exceed spread income in extreme market conditions, and that Variational uses a last-look rejection mechanism as a risk control. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-11) — https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/29532151647170 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
- [statement] Funding and index risk remain even when fees are zero. In Castle Labs' Sept 2026 data snapshot BTC funding ran 1.9% to 7.6% a year on every venue, Lighter's WTI funding reached +95% a year for longs on weekends, venue indices diverged by up to 30 bps on weekends, and pre-IPO perps (Anthropic, OpenAI) differed across venues by 379 and 569 bps. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01) — https://castlelabs.io/research/reports/mapping-the-perpetual-trading-ecosystem · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
- [statement] On Lighter, speed and throughput are the paid features, and the zero fee is paid for with latency. Standard accounts have 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and no maker latency. Premium/Advanced has 140 ms taker latency at 0.004% maker and 0.028% taker, with up to 30% off for 500,000 staked LIT. Plus costs 0.5bps, keeps the 300 ms taker delay, and raises rate limits. LIT fee credits count toward both the fee-discount tier and the rate-limit tier, and their proceeds go to stakers. TrueHold says 300 ms of slippage can exceed the 0.028% taker fee for frequent liquidity takers in fast markets. Cartea et al. model why: during a delay the book can update, so a marketable order may miss its fill or fill at a worse price. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees/lit-fee-credits, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees, https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03281
- [statement] Lighter's LLP is the backstop behind zero-fee trading, so liquidity providers absorb the shock. LLP is the counterparty to all LLP trading and liquidations. ADL starts only when LLP, or the relevant LLP strategy, cannot cover losses. LLP strategies segregate collateral by market group (for example crypto perps, FX, equities/RWA), so losses stay inside one strategy. LLP is open only to LIT stakers, up to 10 USDC deposited per 1 LIT staked. On-Chain Times reported that larger outside market makers had cut LLP's maker share from about 80% to about 7%. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/liquidations-and-llp-insurance-fund/llp-strategies · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/about-lighter/lit-utility, https://www.onchaintimes.com/a-look-into-lighters-llp-recent-performance/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Listing counts increasingly reflect RWA rather than altcoins. one RWA-perps guide's timeline says that on 11 September 2026 perpetual DEXs passed 1,000 listed RWA markets, 747 of them individual shares; Castle Labs reports RWA perps reached $147.5 billion of volume in July 2026, 19.6% of all onchain perp volume; and CoinGecko, citing DefiLlama data, says Variational grew from 6 to over 119 TradFi markets between May and September. The example is a vendor illustration. Regular to VIP 3 users continue to receive a 20% discount on taker fees and VIP 4 to 9 users a 50% discount, compared to the standard USDT taker fee rate. Its table lists 0.0000% maker for Regular User and VIP 1 to VIP 9; taker is 0.0400% (0.0360% with the 10% BNB discount) for Regular User and VIP 1, and 0.0085% (0.0077%) for VIP 9. On 2026-10-28 Binance announced the VIP 4 to 9 discount would be reduced from 50% to 40% with effect from 2026-11-05 08:00 (UTC); the 2026-11-04 notice says that change will not be implemented. - [statement] Bitfinex's announcement of Wednesday, December 17, 2025 says fees for all maker and taker activity on Bitfinex platforms will no longer be charged, effective immediately, with zero fees applying to products including derivatives trading. Its fee schedule lists derivatives trades with maker fees Zero and taker fees Zero. The Zero Fees Q&A says this is not a short term promotion, that there is no fixed end date, and that zero maker and taker fees apply to all trading pairs within the eligible product categories. - [statement] Check the fee your API orders actually pay before sizing a strategy on a zero-fee headline. MEXC's own API comparison tells readers to check each venue's API fee schedule before deploying, because it can differ from the fee page; KCEX's blog says a trader who builds a bot using a promotional web fee may discover that the API has a separate schedule; Bitfinex's summary endpoint documents DERIV_TAKER_FEE and DERIV_REBATE; and Binance's change log lists the GET /fapi/v1/commissionRate endpoint to get user commission rate.
