- [statement] Standard accounts face a 60 requests per rolling minute REST limit, unweighted. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and Builder accounts (free, applied for via Discord) get 240,000. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405. A firewall block lasts 60 seconds; an API-server cooldown follows `weightOfEndpoint/(totalWeight/60)`. Opening a WebSocket (weight 90) counts against the REST limit. Authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply instead of IP-based limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
- [statement] Lighter mainnet and Lighter on Robinhood Chain have separate base URLs and rate-limit tables. In the Robinhood Chain tables, Standard has 200 ms maker/cancel latency and 8 sub-accounts, Plus pays 0.015% with 8000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 120000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium fees and limits follow last 14D volume (0.0120% maker, 0.0350% taker below $1M) instead of staked LIT. - [statement] In October 2025 Lighter said a runaway bot jammed through the HYPE book with size, that there were no liquidations or other adverse effects, and that the wick was scrubbed from the front end. - [statement] The 'zero fee is a latency tax' critique is a model, not a measurement. A MarsBit article (last updated on 2025-12-11) puts the standard account's actual cost at 6-12 basis points per trade versus 0.2-2 basis points on the premium account (5-10 times higher), using typical volatility levels (50–80% annualized) and an informed-trader advantage of 2–5 times. Leviathan News repeated the 5–10× claim on its X account. TrueHold frames the trade-off as a choice: a $10,000 position opened and closed with market orders costs $0 on a Lighter standard account and $5.60 on Premium before discounts, and 300 ms of slippage can cost more than a 0.028% taker fee for traders who take liquidity often in fast markets. (medium confidence) — https://www.htx.com/news/the-illusion-of-zero-fees-how-lighter-extracts-costs-through-SkcqJ0ec/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/leviathan_news/status/1999011488283914615, https://www.truehold.xyz/blog/lighter-fees, https://docs.lighter.xyz/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] Lighter auth tokens are signed with an API key and each can have a maximum expiry of 8 hours, with the structure {expiry_unix}:{account_index}:{api_key_index}:{random_hex}. REST sends the token as the Authorization header; WebSocket sends it as "auth" inside the subscribe message. Authenticating a request makes it count against the L1 address instead of the IP. Read-only tokens (structure ro:{account_index}:{single|all}:{expiry_unix}:{random_hex}) cannot sign transactions, have a maximum expiry of 10 years and a minimum of 5 minutes, and cover one account index (single) or the master account and its sub-accounts (all). On Lighter, tokens/create costs 10,000 request weight, so create tokens once and store them. Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/ai-and-agents/agent-instructions.md
- [statement] Hard-coded numbers in third-party connectors can disagree with Lighter's docs. Hummingbot's Lighter connector constants say the table matches the docs exactly, yet encode Plus sendTx at 8,000 per minute, a Plus read pool of 120,000 weighted requests and Premium sendTx of 4,000–40,000 depending on staked LIT. Lighter's mainnet docs list Plus at 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium up to 72000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute. Read the live docs instead of copying numbers. - [statement] Aster's API limits are tracked per IP (the header X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT shows request weight used by your IP) and the order rate limit is counted against each account (X-MBX-ORDER-COUNT header). Breaching a limit returns HTTP 429, ignoring 429s triggers an automated IP ban (HTTP 418) that scales in duration from 2 minutes to 3 days, and HTTP 503 means the execution status is UNKNOWN rather than a failure. The docs recommend WebSocket streams over REST polling. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md
- [statement] EdgeX's V2 API has public endpoints (metadata, quotes, funding; no authentication required) and private REST and WebSocket endpoints that need a signature-based authentication mechanism, plus an EIP-712 Layer 2 signature for trading operations. Official Python and Go SDKs exist, production REST is at https://edgex-prod-v2.edgex.exchange and WebSocket at wss://edgex-quote-prod-v2.edgex.exchange, and the docs note SDK coverage may differ from the full platform endpoint set. - [statement] Nado's gateway rate limits are weight-based: IP addresses have a max weight limit of 2400 per minute or 400 every 10 seconds applied only to queries, wallet addresses 600 per minute or 100 every 10 seconds applied only to executes, and users can have up to 500 open orders per subaccount per market. Placing orders without spot leverage is limited to 30 per minute or 5 every 10 seconds because those orders are 20x more expensive to place, versus 600 per minute with spot leverage. The sequencer is described as striking the orderbook at 5-15 ms latency with settlement via the Ink L2. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.nado.xyz/developer-resources/api/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.nado.xyz/, https://nadohq.github.io/nado-python-sdk/index.html, https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/tree/master/python/ccxt
- [statement] Several venues expose a machine-readable fee query, so a bot can read effective rates at startup instead of hard-coding them: Aster GET /fapi/v1/commissionRate (HMAC SHA256), Extended GET /api/v1/user/fees, Decibel GET /api/v1/user_fee_rates, Nado's Fee Rates query (IP weight = 2), Hibachi's public exchange-info response (a feeConfig object with tradeMakerFeeRate and tradeTakerFeeRate), Arcus GET /v1/markets/feeSchedules, and EdgeX contract metadata (defaultMakerFeeRate and defaultTakerFeeRate per contract). Arcus' docs state rates can change without a release. - [statement] Aster's V3 futures API documents two per-minute limiters in exchangeInfo: REQUEST_WEIGHT with a limit of 2400 and ORDERS with a limit of 1200, and the order rate limit is counted against each account. Breaking a limit returns HTTP 429, and continuing to send after 429s triggers an automated IP ban (HTTP 418) whose length scales from 2 minutes to 3 days. The docs advise reading order status and position updates from the WebSocket user data stream rather than REST endpoints, because REST responses can be delayed during extreme market volatility. - [statement] Bullet offers post-only variants: its order types are Limit (GTC), Fill or Kill (FOK), Immediate or Cancel (IOC), Post Only, Post-Only Slide and Post-Only Front. In the API, PostOnly is rejected if it would immediately match, PostOnlySlide slides to the best non-crossing price instead of rejecting, and PostOnlyFront posts at the front of the queue at the best price that doesn’t cross; orders also take reduce_only, client_order_id and an attached take-profit / stop-loss pair. Time In Force and TWAP are listed as Coming Soon. - [statement] If an account exceeds the Retail rate limits it automatically switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity; over WebSocket a Retail order over its limit is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits
- [statement] Over-limit behavior differs by channel. On REST, a Retail account that exceeds the Retail limits automatically switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity. On WebSocket, Retail order.create, order.create_batch and order.modify carry an extra per-account limit (10 req/s OR 10 req/m OR 100 req/h OR 2000 req/24h) and an over-limit order is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior. REST order requests also count toward the WebSocket order limit, and a batch request counts as one request. A request over the limit is rejected with error code 42901. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/blob/main/agents/learnings/websocket-errors-rate-limits.md, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/611fbf4133673333fcb65b87d346c2b15767d00a
- [statement] Paradex says it funds zero retail fees from RPI (Retail Price Improvement) maker flow rather than from retail takers: professional makers post RPI orders that are visible in the UI and hidden from the API, they match only retail takers, and makers pay 0.5 bps on RPI fills; the launch blog added that high-frequency API takers pay 2 bps and that toxicity-based fees would follow. Delphi Digital and Alea Research independently describe this flow segmentation as payment for order flow (PFOF). DefiLlama's protocol page lists Fees 30d of $33,929 and Perp Volume 30d of $241.59m. - [statement] Retail orders carry a 300ms speed bump on submission and on cancellation. The Retail limits are 3 orders / sec, 30 orders / min, 300 orders / hr and 1,000 orders / 24 hrs, against 800 orders / sec and 17,250 orders / min for Pro. An account that exceeds the Retail limits switches to Pro Order behavior and loses access to RPI liquidity. Over WebSocket a Retail Order over its limit is rejected rather than switched to Pro Order behavior, with error code 42901. A docs commit of 30 Oct 2025 raised the retail activity thresholds from 10 orders / minute, 60 orders / hour and 750 orders / 24 hours to 30 orders / minute, 300 orders / hour and 1000 orders / 24 hours. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.paradex.trade/ws/general-information/rate-limits, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/065e93dd274b1352dd4ea6fe51ba9d375bbccbef, https://github.com/tradeparadex/paradex-docs/commit/53388a63ab02b88ef757c742fa4bb9edea5504ce
- [statement] Post-only means cancel-on-cross, not slide-to-touch, on all three venues. Lighter cancels a Post-Only limit order if crossing orders exist at placement. Paradex cancels a post-only order that would immediately match. Hyperliquid's API says an ALO order will be canceled instead of immediately matching and lists the error 'Post only order would have immediately matched, bbo was {bbo}.' A converted strategy therefore gets a cancelled order, not a fill, whenever its limit price is marketable on arrival, and must reprice or skip. - [statement] The practical protocol is a bracket, not a point estimate. The vendor article says a maker strategy is deployable only if it survives at the conservative edge of the bracket of fill rules. hftbacktest's RiskAverseQueueModel is its most conservative queue model. Nautilus offers a queue_position option for displayed-queue tracking and warns that a print proves that liquidity existed momentarily, not that it stayed available. Moallemi and Yuan, as cited by the vendor, find that for large-tick instruments the value of a front-of-queue position versus back-of-queue is comparable to the half-spread. - [statement] CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said crypto onchain platforms looking to offer derivatives to US retail traders can register as an exchange or partner with one that is already registered, pointing to Backpack, which earlier that week received three licenses for its US entry, as an example of the first route. He also explained why the agency considers single-stock perpetuals futures rather than swaps, saying funding payments are very similar to variation margin with other types of futures contracts and the contracts are structured as futures, not as a swap or a security-based swap. - [statement] A single-author SSRN preprint reports that Kalshi launched the first CFTC-regulated perpetual futures on 3 June 2026, and that through 20 September 2026 39% of BTC and 48% of ETH notional was executed in resting quotes of a fixed dollar size taken in full by orders of the same size. - [statement] Variational's zero fee is paid through the spread. Omni charges no trading fees and takes its revenue from the spread captured by the Omni Liquidity Provider (OLP). The OLP is a market-making desk run by the founding team that stands opposite all traders and hedges on other venues. The protocol receives a cut of OLP spread revenue instead of a cut of fees. Costs outside the trade price are a flat $0.1 per deposit or withdrawal and a liquidation penalty at ask +0.5% (short) or bid -0.5% (long). - [statement] In the October 2025 liquidation event, tail losses landed on different parties at Lighter and Hyperliquid. Lighter's LLP lost about 5% (5.35% per Phemex) while Lighter kept providing liquidity instead of using ADL, and an outage lost three transaction batches. Hyperliquid's HLP made over $40 million (Kappa Lab), but Hyperliquid's ADL closed $2.1 billion of positions in 12 minutes. Chitra estimates that profitable traders lost between $45.0M and $51.7M more than the minimum haircut needed to cover the shortfall. Chitra also proves that no ADL policy can satisfy exchange solvency, revenue and fairness at once. Someone pays: LLP depositors on one design, profitable traders on the other. (medium confidence) — https://phemex.com/news/article/lighter-exchange-outage-amid-19b-crypto-liquidation-28446 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://www.onchaintimes.com/a-look-into-lighters-llp-recent-performance/, https://kappalab.io/insights/hlp-vs-llp-how-perpetual-dex-vaults-performed-in-the-20b-crypto-crash-october-2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01112

- [statement] Hyperliquid's HIP-3 requires a deployer to hold 500k HYPE staked (maintained for a minimum of 183 days after the dex is deployed) to deploy one perp dex with independent margining and order books. The first 3 assets deployed in any perp dex need no auction participation; additional assets go through a Dutch auction. A deployer can settle an asset with the `haltTrading` action at the current mark price and reuse it, and once all assets are settled the required stake is free to be unstaked. Validators can slash a deployer's stake for malicious market operation. - [statement] Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts are gated by a volume quota that is enforced only for those tiers. Only L2CreateOrder, L2CancelAllOrders, L2ModifyOrder and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume quota; single-order cancels do not. Quota is earned per fill at 1 quota per $1 or $2 of notional depending on the market, shared across sub-accounts of one L1 address, and every 15 seconds the account gets one free sendTx. A sendTxBatch of n transactions consumes n quota. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits
- [statement] Per-account order caps differ by tier. Standard allows 50 pending (TP/SL/TWAP) and 250 active orders per account, with 10 pending and 30 active per market. Premium/Advanced allows 1000 pending and 1500 active per account, with 100 pending and 1000 active per market. Transaction-type limits apply to all tiers, for example 40 requests/minute by default and for L2UpdateLeverage, and 2 requests/minute plus 3 per 2 hours for L2Withdraw. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
- [statement] API trading goes through the sendTx and sendTxBatch REST endpoints or the jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch WebSocket types. Every transaction is signed with SignerClient, which uses a signer binary whose code is in the public lighter-go repo. Each order carries a nonce, integer prices and sizes, and a client order index unique across all markets. HTTP code=200 only means the syntax was accepted; the sequencer can still reject the order. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/signing-transactions · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/blob/main/lighter/signer_client.py, https://github.com/smohantty/lighter-trading-bot
- [statement] On 16 Nov 2026 one transfer of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC (about 10.39 million USDC) left Lighter's Ethereum contract to a single wallet, which Bitquery traced through CoW Swap to ETH and on toward Hyperliquid. Lighter said its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure and official SDKs were not compromised. Lighter paused withdrawals and pool creation and switched on Guardian mode; Guardian mode was later disabled, withdrawals resumed, and its Security Council returned approximately $5 million in USDC to the affected trader. (high confidence) — https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://mlq.ai/news/crypto-exchange-lighter-pauses-withdrawals-after-about-10-million-is-drained-through-a-leaked-api-key/, https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/
- [statement] Per Lighter's postmortem as reported by Crypto Briefing, the affected accounts used signing code outside the official SDKs that repeatedly reused cryptographic nonces, so private keys could be reconstructed from publicly available signatures. The attacker used the keys to create a public pool from the affected account, acquired pool shares through a separate account, transferred the victim's funds into the pool and redeemed the shares. (medium confidence) — https://cryptobriefing.com/lighter-api-key-security-exploit/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://www.blockhead.co/2026/11/18/api-keys-are-the-new-hot-wallet-lighter-luxor-and-signalplus-show-how-credentials-beat-contracts/
- [statement] After the incident Lighter requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools and made API key signatures nonpublic. It plans to introduce IP allowlists, configurable API key permissions and automated monitoring for nonce reuse, and advised traders using custom or third party signing software to rotate their API keys and switch to its official SDKs. Lighter's documentation says API keys can place trades, manage positions and move funds between accounts tied to the same wallet, as reported by Cointelegraph via MLQ. - [statement] Transaction-type limits apply beyond the tier buckets: a default of 40 requests per minute, L2Withdraw 2 per minute and 3 per 2 hours, L2UpdateLeverage 40 per minute, L2ChangePubKey 300 per minute and L2Transfer 120 per minute. NautilusTrader reports that amending on every quote drift hit Lighter Mainnet `code=23000` (`Too Many Requests`) after roughly 40 modifications in a minute, and advises setting `sendtx_quota_per_min` to 40 or lower for transaction-heavy quoting. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md
- [statement] Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts, not Standard, are gated by a volume quota. Only L2CreateOrder, L2CancelAllOrders, L2ModifyOrder and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume it (a batch of n transactions consumes n; single-order cancels are free). New accounts start at 1,000 quota and switching up from Standard resets it to 1,000. Most markets earn 1 quota per $1 of fill notional, but BTC, ETH and SOL stay at the $2 default of 1 quota per $2. Quota is shared across sub-accounts, a free transaction is granted every 15 seconds, trading alone refills it up to 15,000,000, and Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can buy it through POST /api/v1/buyVolumeQuota at $500 per 1M quota. No-fill quote refreshes can exhaust it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/193, https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md
- [statement] Lighter's /changeAccountTier endpoint switches account tiers. Upgrades can happen at any time, and downgrades require a 24-hour cooldown after the last tier change and a sub-account count that fits the lower tier. Since an August 2026 announcement, changing account type no longer requires closing positions or orders. The endpoint weighs 3000, which allows a maximum of 8 requests per rolling minute, and switching from Standard to Plus or Premium/Advanced resets the volume quota for the L1 address to 1,000. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/rate-limits · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/account-types
- [statement] If the API accepted a transaction with code 200 but the outcome is unknown (timeout, dropped connection, no WebSocket confirmation), do not re-sign blindly. Check the transaction status by hash or the account_tx channel and compare nextNonce with the nonce you used. Re-signing with a new nonce while the original may still execute can place the order twice, and reusing the same clientOrderIndex rejects a second order only while the first is still open. NautilusTrader retains pending state on ambiguous delivery for reconciliation and does not resend the batch, and lighter-python issue 193 (open, with no comments) asks for an authoritative crash-safe recovery procedure and the meaning of the numeric status values. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://nautilustrader.io/docs/md/latest/integrations/lighter.md, https://github.com/elliottech/lighter-python/issues/193
- [statement] Lighter's postmortem guidance for programmatic traders: sign with an official Lighter SDK (Python, Go, TypeScript or the Agent Kit), which generate every nonce with a cryptographically secure random number generator. With your own or third-party signing code, never derive a nonce from a timestamp, a counter, a weakly seeded random number generator, the transaction's contents or a cached value. Store keys securely and never share them or commit them to code repositories. If you are unsure whether your code has ever reused a nonce, rotate all of your API keys and switch to an official SDK. GoPlus adds that fixing the code alone isn't enough (revoke and replace all related API keys) and recommends enabling IP allowlisting and per-key permissions and limits as they become available. Lighter's API-keys docs separately say to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/GoPlusSecurity/status/2122520900046319815, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/integration-guides/api-keys.md, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md
- [statement] Do not confuse the two nonces. The nonce in the Lighter incident is a one-off random value used by each signature: if the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. The transaction nonce in the SDK docs is tracked per API key, and failed transactions are re-signed starting from the current nextNonce. GoPlus states that signing nonces are distinct from transaction nonces. (medium confidence) — https://x.com/GoPlusSecurity/status/2122520900046319815 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717, https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md
- [statement] Per Lighter's August 2026 announcement, public pools can be created after reaching $10M in traded volume via a Plus or Premium account, without any sort of whitelist required. The November 16 attack used a public pool created from the affected account, and Lighter temporarily suspended all withdrawals and pool creation in a post at 11:02 UTC. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-30) — https://t.me/lighter_api_updates/168 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/article/2122394446343946717, https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122311006604984497
- [statement] After the November 16 incident, Lighter's smart contract Guardian temporarily paused withdrawals and allowed ~5MM USDC to be returned to the affected trader by the Lighter Security Council; Guardian mode was then disabled, and Lighter announced that deposits and withdrawals were back to normal. Lighter now requires a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool. Sig and L1Sig inside info now return empty strings in transaction responses (tx, txFromL1TxHash, txs, accountTxs, blockTxs, block, blocks and account WebSocket channels), so identify transactions by hash and check their state using status. - [statement] A report relayed by Phemex says arb.sh founder 0xTria revealed that a Relay solver stalled during frozen withdrawals and then repeatedly executed backlogged payments upon resuming at 19:14 UTC, generating 395 duplicate transfers within 25 minutes, totaling approximately $527,000 across 10 accounts. (low confidence) — https://phemex.com/news/article/relay-solver-glitch-triggers-527k-duplicate-withdrawals-on-lighter-dex-103904 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API
- [statement] Lighter's own post-mortem, which a Cryptonews article says was published at 18:20 UTC on November 16, 2026, says an attacker gained control of a trader's API keys on the morning of November 16 (UTC) and withdrew funds. Lighter says its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. It says the keys leaked through the affected accounts' own signatures: the accounts used unsafe signing code other than the official Lighter SDKs, and that code reused signing nonces, which made the private keys recoverable from public data. Lighter says its official SDKs (Python, Go, TypeScript or the Agent Kit) generate every nonce with a cryptographically secure random number generator and were not affected. (high confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122394446343946717 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://cryptonews.net/news/security/33769460/
- [statement] Per Lighter, an API key can send funds to its own account's sub-accounts, and a public pool the account creates counts as one. The attacker used the leaked key to create a public pool from the affected account, mint pool shares in a separate, attacker-controlled account, transfer the affected account's funds into the pool (increasing NAV without minting pool shares), then redeem the shares and withdraw. Lighter says the attacker needed no access to the accounts or to Lighter's systems. (high confidence) — https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122394446343946717 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://cryptonews.net/news/security/33769460/
- [statement] Lighter says it has already required a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool and made API key signatures non-public. It says it is still adding IP whitelists for API keys, permissions and limits configurable per API key (which actions a key may take and which markets it can trade), and monitoring signatures for nonce reuse, contacting affected accounts directly and proactively voiding affected API keys. A republished news report said IP allowlists and configurable permissions for individual keys remain planned. The analysis also says nothing in the post establishes a general compensation policy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-18) — https://cryptonews.net/news/security/33769460/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://bitquery.io/investigations/lighter-hack, https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122394446343946717
- [statement] Lighter uses the word nonce for two different things. In the developer docs it is a per-API-key transaction counter (default new_nonce = previous_nonce + 1). In the post-mortem it is a one-off random value used by each signature, which must be unique and unpredictable; if the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. Lighter says never to derive a signature nonce from a timestamp, a counter, a weakly seeded random number generator, the transaction's contents or a cached value, and to use a cryptographically secure random number generator for every signature. (high confidence) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/getting-started/core-concepts.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://x.com/Lighter_xyz/status/2122394446343946717
- [statement] Volume quota rules for Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts: new accounts start at 1,000 quota, quota does not expire, and switching from Standard to Plus or Premium/Advanced resets the L1 address to 1,000. L2CreateOrder, L2ModifyOrder, L2CancelAllOrders and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume quota; a sendTxBatch of n transactions consumes n, grouped orders consume only one, and single-order cancels consume none. Every 15 seconds the account gets one free sendTx. The authenticated accountLimits endpoint's response schema includes volume_quota_remaining, volume_quota_cap and volume_quota_purchase_cap, together with user_tier_name, current_maker_fee_tick, current_taker_fee_tick and effective_lit_stakes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.lighter.xyz/developers/reference/volume-quota · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API · also: https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/account/accountlimits.md
- [statement] lighter-python's repository page lists v1.1.9 as the latest release, dated Nov 18, 2026, among 25 releases, and requires Python 3.8+. Its nonce manager (pull request 162, opened Jul 6, 2026) fetches nonces lazily on first use per api key and holds a per-api-key asyncio.Lock across nonce assignment and send, so concurrent orders on one key arrive in nonce order while different keys send in parallel. Explicit nonce/api_key_index callers bypass the nonce manager entirely. For the current binary options discovery methods and response models, Lighter's troubleshooting page says to use lighter-sdk 1.1.8 or newer, or lighter-go v1.0.12 or newer. - [statement] Extended's API uses an X-Api-Key header for API access and, for write operations (order management, transfers, withdrawals), also requires a Stark signature generated with the account's private Stark key under the SNIP12 standard (EIP712 for Starknet); you can create up to ten sub-accounts per wallet address, each with its own API and Stark keys. Order placement is asynchronous: an order ID returns immediately, before the order is recorded in the book, and status is tracked on the Order WebSocket stream. REST is throttled per IP at a default of 1,000 requests/minute (Tier 1 4,000 on request, Tier 2 8,000 above $50M and Tier 3 12,000 above $150M of 30-day trading volume), a 429 status code is returned on excess, the User-Agent header is required, and the exchange servers are hosted in the AWS Tokyo region (AZ ap-northeast-1a). The Python SDK is at x10xchange/python_sdk. - [statement] RPI orders are Post-Only maker orders placed on the New Order endpoint with `instruction="RPI"`. The matching engine guarantees they match only Retail Taker orders (orders submitted with an interactive JWT token), never regular API orders; they have the lowest execution priority at their price level, they rest until cancelled even away from the BBO, and they are absent from the API order book, so the UI book can look crossed while the API book stays uncrossed. Delphi's report called RPI a UI-only price-improvement lane; the docs now also count interactive-token API orders as Retail takers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/rpi · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://members.delphidigital.io/reports/paradex-reimagining-on-chain-markets-from-first-principles, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/trader-profiles
- [statement] The Retail-visible book is available over the API: `GET /v1/bbo/{market}/interactive` and `GET /v1/orderbook/{market}/interactive`; the interactive book is what Retail orders see and includes RPI quotes. The orderbook endpoint also carries best_bid_interactive, best_ask_interactive, best_bid_api and best_ask_api size fields. A third-party Rust client lists both interactive endpoints. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/calumrussell/roshar/blob/main/roshar-paradex/README.md · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Paradex zero-fee retail perpetuals and API · also: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/blob/master/ts/src/paradex.ts, https://docs.paradex.trade/trading/fastfills, https://api.prod.paradex.trade/v1/orderbook/BTC-USD-PERP/interactive?depth=100

- [statement] Paradex's Python SDK paradex-py connects with SBE binary encoding by default: public market data always arrives as SBE, private channels (`orders`, `fills`, `positions`, `account`) may arrive as SBE or JSON depending on the account, and `sbe_enabled=False` is for an endpoint that still serves JSON. - [statement] On Jan 19 a planned 30-minute database upgrade went wrong, and per CoinDesk trading resumed at 12:10 UTC after around eight hours of downtime. Paradex's post-mortem says a race condition during a service restart persisted corrupted state and published it to Paradex Chain, so some markets reset the funding index to 0, which created abnormal funding PnL and liquidations. Paradex rolled the chain back to block 1604710 (04:27:54 UTC), cancelled all open orders except TP/SL orders, and refunded $650,000 across 200 accounts from the Liquidator Vault. It was the chain's first rollback. During the post-only period a small number of aggressive orders skewed the mark price and caused additional liquidations, primarily on PAXG. - [statement] Re-pegging a post-only order every few hundred milliseconds re-enters at the back of the queue each time, so its realistic fill profile is mostly adverse selection; queue position is the price of re-quoting. A chase-style convert-to-maker loop for a taker signal therefore trades fill rate against priority. (medium confidence) — https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/ · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2

(low confidence) — https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/6730 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
- [statement] Same-signal comparison from one live experiment on the Binance Bitcoin perpetual (February 12 to 19, 2024, 232,897 minimum-sized maker orders; under its most favorable tier the taker fee is 1.5 bp and the maker fee is -0.5 bp, a rebate). An order-book-imbalance taker strategy earned around +1 bp per roundtrip before fees but -1.9621 after fees (18927 trades). The maker versions of the same signal lost -0.4705 without a cancel rule (8851 trades) and -0.4921 with one (7333 trades), net of fees; a naive maker lost -0.4307. The authors say the maker strategies are primarily undermined by fill probability: they almost always miss out on favorable price moves and keep the fills corresponding to reversals. Latency is ignored there, potentially leading to an overstatement of results. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625v2 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies
- [statement] Queue-aware simulation needs an explicit queue-position model. hftbacktest is replay-based (no market impact) and supports Market-By-Price data; it offers RiskAverseQueueModel (the most conservative: cancellations and modifications in the book happen only at the tail of the queue, and the queue position advances only if a trade happens at the price) and ProbQueueModel (PowerProbQueueFunc and LogProbQueueFunc variants), with NoPartialFillExchange as the default exchange simulation. a vendor article adds that queue position should be seeded at ack time, not decision time, and that a maker strategy is deployable only if it survives at the conservative edge of the bracket of fill rules. (medium confidence) — https://hftbacktest.readthedocs.io/en/latest/order_fill.html · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Post-only maker conversion of taker signal strategies · also: https://marketmaker.cc/blog/fill-simulation-partial-fills-backtest/
- [statement] On Lighter the cancel-on-cross outcome does not appear in the API reply. The docs say an API response with code: 200 means accepted, not executed, and that an order cancelled by matching rules (for example post-only would cross) is a successful transaction that consumes its nonce. A bot must confirm the order's fate on the WebSocket account channels or with GET /api/v1/tx. - [statement] On May 29, 2026 the CFTC approved KalshiEX's BTCPERP as a futures contract under Section 5c(c)(4) of the Commodity Exchange Act and Regulation 40.3. The Order's scope is limited to the BTCPERP Contract and similarly structured perpetual futures referencing bitcoin or other digital commodities, and Katten says the related interpretation does not extend to other asset classes. - [statement] Variational's single-dealer design moves the discipline from competition to exit. Critics quoted by Bankless argue a lone dealer means 'one quote with no competition'; OLP's hedging book is not auditable by outsiders; if OLP became insolvent, later accrued profit would be treated as bad debt and not paid out, while user collateral sits in segregated per-user settlement pools. BlockBeats says OLP uses a 'last-look' rejection control (not mentioned on the Variational fee or OLP docs pages read). Variational's trading API was reported as going first to a small group of alpha testers ahead of a public launch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://docs.variational.io/omni/the-omni-liquidity-provider-olp, https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/29532151647170
- [statement] During the same event Lighter had an outage: three transaction batches were lost, and security firm Beosin attributed it to dependence on a single sequencer and ZK-proof generation bottlenecks while the CEO admitted a delayed database upgrade (single secondary source, PANews via Phemex). (low confidence) — https://phemex.com/news/article/lighter-exchange-outage-amid-19b-crypto-liquidation-28446 · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs
- [statement] A zero fee does not guarantee the cheapest fill at every size: fees dominate small orders and book depth dominates large ones. OpenChainBench states that at $1M notional price impact dwarfs the taker fee, so a zero-fee venue can lose to a 4 bps venue with a deeper book, and that on thin books such as SOL impact can exceed the whole taker fee. It adds that Lighter pays for its 0 bps start with slightly wider spreads on smaller markets. Castle Labs found Hyperliquid had the lowest median slippage at $1M of the five venues it tested on crypto majors: 3.7 bps against 3.8 bps on Binance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://openchainbench.com/benchmarks/perp-fees · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://castlelabs.io/research/reports/mapping-the-perpetual-trading-ecosystem
- [statement] DefiLlama's fee-summary data for Lighter returns daily fee series and per-product methodology text that says what each line counts; for Lighter, liquidation fees are excluded from revenue and routed to LLP, and supply-side revenue is defined as liquidation fees paid to the LLP. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.llama.fi/summary/fees/lighter · keywords: Zero-fee perpetual futures venues with API access, Zero-fee perp venue economics and hidden costs · also: https://api.llama.fi/summary/fees/lighter?dataType=dailyRevenue, https://api.llama.fi/summary/fees/lighter?dataType=dailySupplySideRevenue, https://api.llama.fi/summary/fees/lighter?dataType=dailyHoldersRevenue
